prerequisites: Basics of Calculus, Linear Algebra and Physics, contained in the exams of Calculus I, II, Geometry and Physics.

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the fundamental principles of rigid body mechanics, continuum mechanics, and structural mechanics.
Apply the methods and models of Structural Mechanics to the analysis of structural systems, determining equilibrium conditions, internal forces, stresses, strains, and displacements.
Identify the most appropriate analytical model and critically evaluate the obtained results.
Use the technical terminology of Structural Mechanics correctly when describing and discussing structural problems.
Independently deepen their knowledge of the subject and apply the acquired competences in subsequent courses in structural engineering.

syllabus_topics: Duality principle and the Principle of Virtual Work.
Formulation of the elastic problem for bars and beams.
Principle of Virtual Work and displacement methods.
Kinematics and statics of the Cauchy continuum.
Stress and strain states; equilibrium and compatibility equations.
Linear elastic constitutive law and formulation of the elastic problem.
Solutions for axial loading, bending, shear, and torsion.
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical topics, with discussion and proof of the outcomes
Numerical exercises, with physical interpretation of the outcomes
assessment_rules: Student must obtain a score of 18/30 in the written exam. The written exam includes exercises on structures constituted by beams, and evaluation of the stress field and safety of a cross section of a De Saint Venant beam. The oral exam is about thirty minutes long, covering the theoretical part of the course and applications. The final grade is a combination of both exams.
